solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Run meeting jointly with Chirac, nothing getting resolved (2-5)

indicators.note: to resolve something is to break it down and rework it, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A summit at which the French president chairs a joint meeting and nothing gets settled.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs Chirac with diplomacy, so the name looks like colour; it is in fact six of the seven letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain gloss of the verb: two chairs sharing one meeting between them.

entries.clue: Circus regularly appearing in vineyard (3)

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here the first, third and fifth

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word

annotation.surface: A travelling circus turns up to perform among the vines.
annotation.walkthrough: In wine terms a cru is a vineyard or its grade, as in grand cru.
annotation.definitionFit: A cru is a vineyard, especially a French one of recognised quality.

entries.clue: Awfully laconic description of dunce’s cap (7)

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out wrong

annotation.surface: A painfully terse way of describing the pointed hat a dunce wears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Awfully laconic' reads as an intensifier, awfully meaning very; it is the anagram instruction instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A dunce's cap is a tall cone, so the word that describes it is conical.

entries.clue: A pair of islands bordering round lake in Mayo (5)

indicators.note: the two I's sit on either side of the middle letters, forming its border

annotation.surface: Two islands with a round lake between them, off the west coast of Ireland in County Mayo.
annotation.walkthrough: Mayo looks like the Irish county, and the islands and lake keep it there; it is short for mayonnaise, and aioli is a garlic mayonnaise.
annotation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlicky mayonnaise, so it is a kind of mayo.

entries.clue: Banking quarrel, I anticipate, is much scaled down (7)

indicators.note: the phrase is cut down heavily at both ends, leaving only its middle

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word to the start of the third, outer letters stripped away

annotation.surface: A banker predicts that a dispute will be scaled back a good deal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banking' reads as the finance trade; it means banking on, relying on something. The hidden indicator is unusual: the fodder is shrunk until only the answer is left.
annotation.definitionFit: Banking here is the idiom 'banking on', depending on, so it stands for the adjective meaning dependent.

entries.clue: Once more, we turned on a knight (4)

indicators.note: turned round, so WE runs backwards
in an across clue, placed after: EW goes on the end of A N

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round to EW

annotation.surface: A second time, a group rounds on a knight and attacks him.
annotation.walkthrough: N for knight comes from chess notation, where K is already taken by the king.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean again, afresh.

entries.clue: Resembling maestro at heart, first rate and very musical (5)

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: S is the middle of the seven letters of MAE-S-TRO
A1 = first rate, with the 1 read as I

annotation.surface: A conductor praised as first rate and deeply musical.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very musical' is not an adjective phrase but a pointer: assai is the Italian score marking for very, as in allegro assai.
annotation.definitionFit: Assai is the musical direction meaning very, so it is very in musical language.

entries.clue: European friend keeping seabird forever (9)

indicators.note: the friend holds the seabird inside it

annotation.surface: A friend from the continent who never lets a pet seabird go.
annotation.walkthrough: The seabird goes into the friend, not the European: the E stands alone in front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean for all time, without end.

entries.clue: Body involved in Mozambiquan goings-on (6)

indicators.note: the answer is caught up inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last four letters of the first word plus the first two of the second

annotation.surface: A corpse turns up in the middle of some shady business in Mozambique.
annotation.walkthrough: A quango is a British term for a semi-independent public body funded by government, such as a regulator or advisory board.
annotation.definitionFit: A quango is an official body, a quasi-autonomous non-governmental organisation.

entries.clue: Was first to cross a street — and survived (6)

indicators.note: LED lies across A ST, straddling it on both sides

blocks.note: to be first is to lead, so was first = led

annotation.surface: Someone rushed to be first over the road and lived to tell of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has a pedestrian dashing across the road; 'cross' is not the road but the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to last is to hold out, to survive.

entries.clue: Scotsman greeting state intrigue (11)

blocks.note: Mac, from the Scottish surname prefix, is a nickname for a Scotsman

annotation.surface: A Scotsman hails his country and joins its political plotting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, a Scotsman stating his greeting; it is the noun, a country.
annotation.definitionFit: A machination is a crafty scheme, a piece of intrigue.

entries.clue: Turned to parent, possibly, as embalmer did? (9)

blocks.note: a whimsical reading: made into a mother, a parent
an embalmer preserves a body as a mummy

annotation.surface: A strange tale of someone who became a parent in the manner of an ancient Egyptian undertaker.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is a joke: mummify read as turn into a mummy, in the British sense of mother, rather than an Egyptian corpse.
annotation.definitionFit: An embalmer who preserved a body mummified it.

entries.clue: Underwear you’ll find in Seychelles finally, but not initially (6)

blocks.note: the surface reading: clothes packed for a trip to the islands

blocks.clueFragment: you’ll find in Seychelles finally, but not initially
blocks.note: the setter's reading: look at the letters of the word, where the last one is lower case and the first a capital

annotation.surface: A packing tip about what to wear at the end of a trip to the Seychelles.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters of Seychelles are the joke: its last letter is a small (lower-case) s, its first a capital. 'Smalls' is British slang for underwear.
annotation.definitionFit: Smalls is a British informal word for underclothes.

entries.clue: As eg Newcastle United shirts quietly removed, undressed (7)

indicators.note: the P is taken out of STRIPPED

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music; removed from STRIPPED

annotation.surface: Newcastle players take their shirts off without a fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: Newcastle United play in black-and-white vertical stripes, which is what makes the definition fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Newcastle United's shirts are black and white stripes, so they are striped.

entries.clue: Not drinking in story or gossip (6)

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abstainer sits within the story

annotation.surface: A teetotaller features in a piece of tittle-tattle.
annotation.walkthrough: TT for teetotal is a standard abbreviation; it sits inside TALE as TA-TT-LE.
annotation.definitionFit: Tattle is idle talk about other people, gossip.

entries.clue: Admiring gift, however has mostly attempted to conceal it (7)

indicators.note: one piece holds the other
most of the word, without its last letter
TRIE wraps around BUT, the 'it' of the clue

blocks.note: attempted = tried; mostly drops the final D

annotation.surface: A grudging present: however much one admires the giver, they have tried to hide it.
annotation.walkthrough: The grammar runs backwards from the surface: 'however' is the subject that gets hidden, and 'it' points back to it.
annotation.definitionFit: A tribute is a gift or gesture made to show admiration.

entries.clue: A lack of ceremony if Royal Mint is involved (11)

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: An occasion goes without pomp once the Royal Mint takes part.
annotation.walkthrough: The Royal Mint makes the UK's coins; its pomp-laden name is the fodder, including the small word 'if'.
annotation.definitionFit: Informality is the absence of ceremony or formal manners.

entries.clue: Loudly abused lone criminal (5)

indicators.note: badly treated, so the letters are knocked out of order

annotation.surface: A solitary crook is shouted at and insulted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' next to 'abused' makes it look like a sound-alike clue; it is only F, the musical forte.
annotation.definitionFit: A felon is someone who has committed a serious crime, a criminal.

entries.clue: Place holding final of competition? (5)

indicators.note: to hold is to keep something within you, so the place takes the letter inside it
the last letter of the next word

annotation.surface: A question about where a cup final might be staged.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition, as the question mark hints: an arena is just the place to hold a final.
annotation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue where competitions and finals are held.

entries.clue: Stimulus provided by Marlowe perhaps to audience (6)

indicators.note: as an audience hears it, so the sound counts, not the spelling

annotation.surface: A boost from Christopher Marlowe's plays, performed before an audience.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre and 'audience' point to the playwright Christopher Marlowe; the Marlowe wanted is Philip, Raymond Chandler's private eye, and 'perhaps' flags him as one example of a Philip.
annotation.definitionFit: A fillip is something that gives a lift or boost, a stimulus.

entries.clue: Suddenly appears as saint, free from blemish, on reflection (6)

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front

annotation.surface: A saint without stain materialises, as seen in a mirror.
annotation.walkthrough: The saint comes first and the whole chain is then reversed, so the saint ends up at the tail.
annotation.definitionFit: Erupt as of a rash or a volcano: to burst suddenly into view.

entries.clue: Add small measure of spirits (3)

blocks.note: the verb, as in adding up a bill
a small dram, as of rum or whisky

annotation.surface: An instruction to pour in a little more whisky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Add' is the verb, as in tot up a bill, not the barman's topping up.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the verb for summing figures and the noun for a small dram.

entries.clue: Unpleasant sound pursuing old Norse God (4)

indicators.note: following behind, so DIN comes after O

blocks.note: a din is a harsh noise

annotation.surface: A racket chases after an ancient Norse deity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old Norse' is a phrase, the language, so 'old' seems to belong to the definition; it gives O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the chief of the Norse gods, father of Thor.

entries.clue: Face shocking treatment, in a manner of speaking (7)

blocks.note: dial = face, as in slang or of a clock
ECT = electroconvulsive therapy, electric shock treatment

annotation.surface: Facing electric-shock therapy, figuratively speaking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads as a hedge, so-to-speak; the definition is the phrase without 'in a'.
annotation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional form of a language, a manner of speaking.
